output.brief: The fall in first-contact resolution is almost certainly due to the 14 April Finance change, not the new starters. It cut the credit an agent can apply on a call from £100 to £25, and larger adjustments now go automatically to the Billing Resolution team. The share of billing calls referred rose from 7% to 54% in the same week the dashboard fell. Referred calls resolve at about 33%, against 82% for the rest, and that gap did not change. Referral rates are the same for new and tenured agents (56% vs 53–54%). Tenured agents' FCR fell from 75% to 67%, the same as the site, so the new intake is not the driver. The tariff mix shift is small: tariff calls are 12% of calls and still resolve at 85%. The IVR redesign is not supported as the cause, because it came two weeks after the drop. I'm fairly sure of the main cause, less sure about the minor factors. Next steps: drop the performance-plan proposal, which would punish the wrong people. Agree a revised credit limit with Finance, with post-call sampling. Trial it on two teams for six weeks, tracking FCR and unsupported credits. Ask MI for the breakdown by team, which takes a day. Hold off on the three-month dashboard rebuild.
